name: Entner-Doudoroff Pathway (Non-Phosphorylative)
notes: Non-phosphorylative ED pathway: alternative variant found in Zymomonas mobilis, some archaea (Sulfolobus), and certain Gram-negative bacteria. Operates on unphosphorylated intermediates (glucose → gluconate → KDG) before producing pyruvate. More ATP-efficient than semi-phosphorylative ED since no initial phosphorylation required. Distinguished by gnaD (gluconate dehydratase) instead of edd. Final aldolase step (eda) cleaves KDG to pyruvate and glyceraldehyde (not G3P). Common in organisms with high extracellular glucose and periplasmic glucose oxidation.

nodes.name: quinoprotein glucose dehydrogenase
nodes.notes: Periplasmic enzyme; oxidizes glucose to glucono-δ-lactone using PQQ cofactor

nodes.name: 6-phosphogluconolactonase
nodes.notes: Hydrolyzes glucono-δ-lactone to gluconate; can also work on non-phosphorylated substrate

nodes.name: gluconate dehydratase
nodes.notes: Diagnostic enzyme for non-phosphorylative ED; dehydrates gluconate to KDG (2-keto-3-deoxy-gluconate)

nodes.name: 2-keto-3-deoxy-gluconate aldolase
nodes.notes: Diagnostic aldolase; cleaves KDG to pyruvate and glyceraldehyde (non-phosphorylated product)

edges.notes: KDG intermediate - diagnostic for non-phosphorylative ED

scoring.notes: All 4 steps required for pathway completion. Diagnostic markers (gnaD/eda) distinguish non-phosphorylative ED from semi-phosphorylative ED and other glucose pathways. At least one marker gene must be present. gnaD is the key distinguishing enzyme from semi-phosphorylative ED which uses edd instead.
